history.summary: IMPORTANT CONTEXT: this cycle's local /app-evolve run discovered the hourly cloud routine hit a real problem on its first fire — its ephemeral container found a genuine bug (assetSubline() rounds fractional stockQty/fxAmount via comma()) and committed a fix locally, but git push failed (403, GitHub App not authorized) and the commit was later stranded/lost. After the user reconnected the GitHub App, a second issue surfaced: the routine tried to write .claude/app-evolve/state.json and deadlocked on a permission prompt for 'sensitive' .claude/ paths, with no human present to approve. FIXED as a distinct infrastructure correction: migrated the state file to a plain repo-root app-evolve-state.json (never under .claude/) and updated both the project-level and user-level app-evolve skills to commit it on every phase, including critique/no-op reviews. BANKED for a future develop cycle: re-implement the lost commaQty() display fix. This critique phase's own plan (still valid): add a lightweight Node regression-test suite for the pure-logic functions fixed across cycles 0-4, since there was zero permanent safety net.

Implemented the critique plan: added our-assets-v1.14.1/our-assets/test/run.js, a dependency-free Node regression suite (assert-based, no package.json) that extracts pure-logic function source directly out of index.html via a vm sandbox and runs 15 assertions covering bugs fixed in cycles 0-4 — addMonths month-rollover/leap-year clamping, recDates monthly day-clamp, recNthDate/recCountUntil weekend-adjustment round-trip, num()'s sign-stripping, doRenameCat's catVar/catIcon migration, and activeRecsForAssets. Sanity-checked the harness by reintroducing the old buggy addMonths into a scratch copy — 3 of 15 tests correctly failed, confirming it actually catches regressions. All 15 pass against the real index.html. Added a pointer to the suite in SKILL.md's pre-check step 4. This cycle also self-corrected a stale local git ref (detached HEAD reconciled with main) encountered while committing, unrelated to the earlier lost commit. This advance was executed by the cloud routine, which confirmed both infrastructure fixes worked end-to-end (push succeeded, state file read/written correctly, no permission deadlock).

Re-implemented the banked commaQty display fix that an earlier cloud run had found and lost. assetSubline() ran a.fxAmount/a.stockQty through comma() (always rounds to integer), so fractional holdings (e.g. 1.5 shares, 1250.75 USD) displayed rounded ('2주', '1,251') while assetEval()'s net-worth math already used the unrounded value — a.goldDon on the same line was already shown unrounded, making the inconsistency visible within one function. Added commaQty() (integers behave like comma(), decimals shown as-is up to 4 places) and used it for fxAmount/stockQty. While wiring this into the new test suite, found and fixed a real bug in the test harness itself: extractConst() kept the 'const ' keyword, but Node's vm.runInContext() doesn't attach top-level const/let to the context object (only function declarations and plain assignments do), so anything added via CONSTS was silently unreachable as sandbox.<name> despite 'successful' extraction — stripped the 'const ' prefix so extracted consts become plain global assignments. Added commaQty (and its dependency comma) to CONSTS plus 3 new test cases. Verified: all 18 tests pass, and directly via the real assetSubline() in the browser (stockQty=1.5 -> '1.5주' was '2주'; fxAmount=1250.75 -> 'USD 1,250.75' was 'USD 1,251').
